properties.name: Park Theater
properties.description: Streamline Moderne single-screen cinema opened Aug 21, 1941 (designed by William B. David); closed 2005; bought by the Park Theater Trust in Dec 2021; under renovation as a two-screen cinema, target reopening early 2027. Interior palette originally blues, ivory and maroon; 1941 neon marquee in storage at NeonWorks.
properties.coord_source: US Census geocoder (address interpolation)

people.name: Elwood P. Laws
people.blurb: Walnut Creek theater operator who built the Park in 1941; also built Walnut Creek's El Rey Theater (1937).

people.name: William B. David
people.blurb: Cinema architect who designed 25+ theaters in California and Oregon in the Streamlined Moderne style, including the Park.

people.name: The Park Theater Trust
people.blurb: All-volunteer nonprofit, first convened as a City task force; raised $3M and bought the theater for the community in Dec 2021.

people.name: CinemaSF (Adam Bergeron, Jaimi Holker)
people.blurb: SF historic-cinema operators chosen to run the reopened Park; their first East Bay venue.

people.name: Lafayette-Orinda Presbyterian Church
people.blurb: The newly founded congregation held Sunday services in the theater starting in 1954.

properties.name: Lafayette Library and Learning Center
properties.description: Library opened Nov 14, 2009, designed by Killefer Flammang Architects as a 'contemporary Craftsman' stone-and-wood building stepping down from Mt Diablo Blvd to First St. Its atrium honors Nobel laureate Glenn Seaborg. Built on the site of the 1938-39 WPA Veterans Memorial Building.
properties.coord_source: OSM way/326482972 centroid

people.name: Lafayette Community Foundation
people.blurb: Formed by citizens (via Lafayette Library Vision 2000, 1998) to fund the library; nearly 25% of residents gave $12.7M toward construction.

people.name: Rick & Janet Cronk
people.blurb: Rick spent 30 years building Dreyer's; the couple were approached as the project's first major donors and agreed, saying nothing matters more than educating children.

people.name: Glenn Seaborg
people.blurb: Nobel laureate and 40-year Lafayette resident, honored by the atrium and the Glenn Seaborg Learning Consortium of 12 Bay Area institutions.

people.name: Killefer Flammang Architects
people.blurb: Won the City's design competition, drawing on ideas from 1,000+ residents.

people.name: Don Tatzin
people.blurb: Mayor who signed the City's 2009 support for the Seaborg Consortium; the Don Tatzin Community Hall in the library bears his name.

properties.name: Lafayette Historical Society
properties.description: Began 1967 as a committee of the Lafayette Library Association; incorporated as a nonprofit March 19, 1973. Located in the Library and Learning Center (location approximate).
properties.coord_source: approximate: library building centroid

people.name: Lafayette Historical Society
people.blurb: Runs the town's oral-history archive and the downtown history tour.

properties.name: Lafayette Hillside Memorial (The Crosses of Lafayette)
properties.description: Hillside of thousands of crosses and other symbols on Deer Hill Rd, visible from BART and Hwy 24, begun 2003 and in earnest Nov 11, 2006. The count sign was replaced with 'Remember' in 2022.
properties.coord_source: OSM way/459217544 centroid

people.name: Jeff Heaton
people.blurb: Local contractor who planted the first 19 crosses in spring 2003 and relaunched the memorial on Armistice Day 2006.

people.name: John & Louise Clark
people.blurb: Longtime residents who allowed the memorial on their hillside.

people.name: Mt. Diablo Peace and Justice Center / Lamorinda Peace Group
people.blurb: Groups that helped build and plant thousands of crosses.

properties.name: Lafayette Reservoir
properties.description: EBMUD reservoir. Dam built 1927-1933 after a 1928 slide forced a lower, wider redesign. Opened for recreation June 13, 1966, with a 2.7-mile paved loop.
properties.coord_source: OSM way/27877916 centroid

people.name: EBMUD
people.blurb: East Bay Municipal Utility District (organized 1923) built the reservoir and opened it to the public in 1966.

people.name: George Pollock Company
people.blurb: Low bidder awarded the dam contract in July 1927 for $1,370,685.

people.name: Leo J. Coleman
people.blurb: Tumbled down the dam face while walking it in the dark on the night of the first cracks, in Sept 1928.

people.name: Lafayette Improvement Club (Rodebaugh, Garrett, Stanley, Meredith)
people.blurb: Formed the Lafayette County Water District to bring Mokelumne water, which led Lafayette into EBMUD.

properties.name: Lafayette Reservoir Outlet Tower
properties.description: Dam outlet tower with valves and pipes to the filter plant. The original plan for a dam 33 ft taller was abandoned, so the tower stands well above the water.

properties.name: Lafayette Reservoir Visitor Center / boat rental
properties.description: Visitor center and boat rental on the north shore.
properties.coord_source: OSM way/348816503 centroid

properties.name: Lafayette Reservoir Rim Trail
properties.description: Rim trail circling the reservoir ridge. The centroid here is from a single OSM segment.
properties.coord_source: OSM way centroid (segment)

properties.name: Lafayette BART station
properties.description: Opened May 21, 1973. One island platform in the Hwy 24 median.
properties.coord_source: Nominatim OSM node/257088282

properties.name: Veterans Memorial Center
properties.description: New Veterans Memorial Center, dedicated May 30, 2005. It replaced the 1938-39 WPA building, whose site became the library.
properties.coord_source: Nominatim OSM node/5889459287

people.name: Works Progress Administration
people.blurb: New Deal program that built the original 1938-39 Veterans Memorial Building at Mt Diablo Blvd and First St.

people.name: Lafayette, Walnut Creek & Contra Costa County
people.blurb: Jointly built the 2005 replacement.

properties.name: Lafayette Plaza
properties.description: Historic triangular town square at Mt Diablo Blvd and Moraga Rd. Elam Brown deeded the land in 1864; redesigned 1998-2001. Pony Express riders changed horses at this intersection in the early 1860s.
properties.coord_source: approximate: Nominatim Plaza Drive

people.name: Elam Brown
people.blurb: Deeded the plaza triangle to the town in 1864.

properties.name: Pioneer Store (Benjamin Shreve's store)
properties.description: Shreve's store, post office and insurance agency, opened in the early 1860s; much remodeled with a false front. Named the Pioneer Store by Robert Elam McNeil in 1902.
properties.coord_source: US Census geocoder (matched Plaza Dr; verify)

people.name: Benjamin Shreve
people.blurb: Stayed after the Gold Rush, ran the first school, named the town 'La Fayette' when Centerville was taken, and was postmaster for 30 years.

properties.name: Town Hall Theatre
properties.description: Built 1914 at School St and Moraga Rd by volunteers and the Lafayette Improvement Association. Theater use began with the Lafayette Playshop in 1941.
properties.coord_source: OSM node/368171449

people.name: Lafayette Improvement Association
people.blurb: Civic group that built the hall in 1914 with community volunteers.

properties.name: Lafayette United Methodist Church
properties.description: The congregation moved in 1927 into the former 1893 third school building on Moraga Rd.
properties.coord_source: US Census geocoder (address interpolation)

properties.description: Middle school named for M.H. Stanley.
properties.coord_source: OSM way/31426940 centroid

people.name: Matthew Howard 'M.H.' Stanley
people.blurb: Lafayette businessman and school-board member who helped expand local schools.

properties.name: Acalanes High School

properties.name: Lafayette Community Center
properties.description: City community center in Burton Valley.
properties.coord_source: Nominatim OSM way/508537765

properties.name: Lafayette Chamber of Commerce
properties.description: Launched in 1947 by local businesspeople.

people.name: Lafayette Chamber of Commerce
people.blurb: Founded 1947; a supporter of the Park Theater rescue.

properties.name: Lafayette-Moraga Regional Trail (Lafayette segment)
properties.description: Rail-trail on the former Sacramento Northern right-of-way (passenger service ended 1941, freight 1957). Dedicated July 4, 1976.
properties.coord_source: Nominatim OSM way/464374988

people.name: Avon Wilson & Lynn Hiden ('the Bike Ladies')
people.blurb: Started the early-1970s bike-safety push that produced the trail.

people.name: East Bay Regional Park District
people.blurb: Partnered with Lafayette and Moraga in the Trails Advisory Committee and manages the trail.
